description:
Goal

Make an uncalled first-class named function value observably identical across the backend interpreter, JIT, and AOT. The value is explicitly first-class and boxed even though no call supplies argument producers; absence of direct invocation is not absence of the function value.

Signal

The minimized source

fn identity(x), do: x
fn main(), do: dbg(identity)

prints null in the backend interpreter and #fn<0/0> in JIT and AOT. Callable-flow evidence has no direct target, as expected, and carries an explicit first-class edge to the boxed resolution. The discrepancy is therefore downstream of valid first-class authority.

Strategy

Trace the first-class FunctionRef value through backend packaging and interpreter materialization, compare it with the native boxed callable path, and establish the intended language-level function-value representation from existing called and uncalled function controls. Repair the first backend representation boundary that loses the value. Do not invent a direct call edge, synthesize argument evidence, or special-case dbg formatting.

Acceptance

The minimized uncalled function, a called named reference, a captured lambda, and an opaque first-class control produce path-invariant behavior on interp, run, and build. Explicit first-class flow remains boxed without direct-target fabrication. Library tests and strict clippy pass.
title: Make uncalled first-class function values path-invariant
